svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Population nine, queue one hundred and fifty
svg.desc: Black-and-white pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon set in a tiny Western Australian Wheatbelt town. Grain silos and wheat paddocks stretch to the horizon, and an old weatherboard hall carries a For Sale by the Shire sign marked Sold. A long queue of city house-hunters with suitcases, takeaway coffees and laptop bags winds down the gravel road from the horizon to the hall steps. On the left, a fictional weathered farmer in a wide-brimmed hat stands with his kelpie by a town sign reading Buntine, population 51 crossed out and 9 written in, saying: first town meeting in years and we've sold the hall. A city woman with a coffee asks: is it walkable to a flat white? A signpost points to Dalwallinu 38 and Perth 280.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY
POPULATION: NINE. QUEUE: ONE HUNDRED AND FIFTY.
Source: ABC News, 25 November 2026 — A Wheatbelt shire sold two old buildings in Buntine for under $100,000 combined.
